lane: Canva Connect API (REST, canva.dev) — with the two adjacent Canva surfaces that the Connect docs point to when content editing is asked about: the Apps SDK Design Editing API and the Canva remote MCP server (mcp.canva.com)

claims.claim: The Connect REST API has NO endpoint that edits design content (text, images, element positions, hyperlinks). The full endpoint index lists only: Authentication, Analytics, Assets, Autofill, Brand Templates, Comments, Designs (create/list/get/pages/export formats/dataset), Design Imports, Exports, Folders, Merges, Resizes, Users, Webhooks.

The Connect changelog (2024-06-18 through 2026-08-25) contains no entry for a Connect-side Design Editing API or any element-level editing; 2026 entries are autofill (create_from_design / update_design GA 2026-08-25), Get design dataset GA, Get design export formats GA, email HTML export formats.

The 'Design Editing API' announced 2025 belongs to the Apps SDK (JavaScript running inside the Canva editor as an app), not to Connect. It moved 'from beta to GA' on Jun 25, 2025 ('The Design Editing API gives your app DOM-like powers to read and modify Canva designs').

Apps SDK Design Editing (openDesign): `current_page` context is GA; `all_pages` context is 'currently in preview and only available in the preview package'. Sessions have a 1-minute expiry; only one page can be loaded at a time. Elements that can be read/created/edited: text, rect (with solid colour or image/video fill), shape (SVG paths), group, embed. Images and videos are represented as rects with media fills; tables 'not currently supported'. Pages cannot be added from openDesign. Element creation via session.helpers.elementStateBuilder.createTextElement / createRectElement / createShapeElement / createEmbedElement, inserted with session.page.elements.insertAfter, saved with await session.sync().

Apps SDK openDesign createTextElement formatting documented on the guide page is fontSize, color, fontWeight, textAlign. fontRef and link are NOT shown for elements created inside openDesign on that page — hyperlink/font-by-ref support for openDesign-created text could not be confirmed from the guide.

Apps SDK addPage (GA, no preview label) adds a page after the current one with custom dimensions (each side 40–8000 px, area ≤ 25,000,000) and accepts text, image, video, shape, group, embed and richtext elements. Text formatting fields include fontRef, fontSize, color, link, textAlign, decoration, fontWeight, fontStyle; image elements take ref, top, left, width, height, altText (+ rotation). Positions -32768..32767 px, dimensions 0..32767 px. Shapes: 1–30 paths, ≤ 2 KB combined, ≤ 6 unique fills.

Apps SDK editContent (GA): target 'current_page' only; only 'richtext' content type; inline formatting includes color, fontWeight, fontStyle, decoration, strikethrough, lineHeightEm 0.5–2.5, letter spacing, `link` ('An external URL that the text links to'), `fontRef`; paragraph formatting includes textAlign, list markers, fontSize 1–1000 px. Cannot add elements or pages.

Apps SDK fonts: findFonts returns 'Only a subset of Canva's fonts'; a FontRef is 'A unique identifier that points to a font asset in Canva's backend'; requestFontSelection returns {ref, name, weights}. Whether Baskerville (Regular/SemiBold/Bold) exists in Canva's library, and whether brand-kit/uploaded fonts are exposed to these APIs, is not stated.

Apps SDK image upload (upload()): 'Maximum file size: 50MB'; MIME types image/jpeg, image/heic, image/png, image/svg+xml, image/webp, image/tiff; the URL 'Must be publicly accessible (i.e. not a localhost URL)' and 'Must not redirect'; thumbnail URL must be HTTPS+CORS, or a base64 data URL ≤ 10 MB.

A developer can run their own Apps SDK app inside the Canva editor without Canva review: 'In the Developer Portal, click the Preview button. This will open the app in a new tab.' (Development URL field). No plan-tier requirement for Preview is stated. Team apps (unreviewed release to a whole team) are Enterprise-only; public release requires Canva app review.
claims.gate: Preview: developer's own account, no review, no stated plan gate. Team apps: Enterprise only. Public: Canva review.

claims.claim: Connect integrations are Public or Private. 'Private integrations can only be used by your team on a Canva Enterprise plan.' Public integrations need Canva review only to be released to all users; 'Public integrations can be used in draft state for individual usage and testing. Unless your integration will be accessed in a marketplace, you don't need to submit it for verification and approval.' So a Pro user creates a PUBLIC integration, leaves it in draft, and authorizes it with his own account.
claims.gate: Private = Enterprise only; Public-in-draft = any plan, no review

claims.claim: Public integrations that use preview APIs 'will not pass the review process', and preview APIs 'are not finalized and we don't recommend them for use in production' — irrelevant to a draft integration used privately, but note Get design pages is still preview.

OAuth: Authorization Code + PKCE (SHA-256); at least one redirect URL must be set; the Quickstart uses http://127.0.0.1:3001/oauth/redirect (plain-HTTP loopback accepted); token exchange must come from a backend (CORS-blocked in browser); access tokens expire in 4 hours (expires_in 14400, 'subject to change'); 'Each refresh token can only be used once'; refresh-token lifetime not documented.

Scopes (18): asset:read, asset:write, brandtemplate:content:read, brandtemplate:content:write, brandtemplate:meta:read, collaboration:event, comment:read, comment:write, design:content:read, design:content:write ('Create designs on the user's behalf'), design:meta:read, email, folder:permission:write, folder:read, folder:write, openid, profile, profile:read. Needed for this kit: asset:write, design:content:write, design:content:read, design:meta:read, folder:read, folder:write.

Create design (POST /v1/designs): preset types doc/email/presentation/whiteboard, or custom width/height in pixels, each 40–8000 px with area ≤ 25,000,000 px² (1296 x 1728 = 2,239,488 fits). Optional asset_id to add one asset — 'Currently, this only supports image assets.' No other content can be specified. 'Blank designs created with this API are automatically deleted if they're not edited within 7 days.' 20 req/min/user.

Asset upload (POST /v1/asset-uploads, application/octet-stream body + Asset-Upload-Metadata header with name_base64, name ≤ 50 chars unencoded) and a URL variant (/v1/url-asset-uploads). Images: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, single-frame GIF, TIFF, single-frame WEBP, 'smaller than 50 MB'; videos < 500 MB. Rate limit 30 req/min/user. Requires asset:write.

Export (POST /v1/exports): formats JPG, PNG, GIF, PPTX, MP4, PDF, CSV, html_bundle, html_standalone. PDF: export_quality 'regular' (default) or 'pro' ('Premium quality export'); 'size' (a4/a3/letter/legal) applies only to Canva Docs; 'pages' array. 'A pro export might fail if the design contains premium elements and the calling user ... isn't on a Canva plan (such as Canva Pro) that has premium features.' No CMYK/bleed/crop-mark/flatten options documented. Limits: 20 req/min/user; 750 exports per 5 min and 5,000 per 24 h per integration; 75 per 5 min per document; 75 per 5 min and 500 per 24 h per user; download URLs valid 24 h. Free plan cannot upscale fixed-dimension designs beyond 1.125x.
claims.gate: 'pro' quality with premium elements: paid plan

claims.claim: Design import (POST /v1/imports, octet-stream body + Import-Metadata header title_base64 / mime_type) and URL import (GA 2025-06-24). Supported types include Adobe Illustrator (application/illustrator, .ai), Photoshop, Affinity, Keynote/Numbers/Pages, Excel/PowerPoint/Word, OpenOffice, PDF. 'Imports with a large number of pages or assets are split into multiple designs.' Response gives design IDs plus edit/view URLs valid 30 days. 20 req/min/user; scope design:content:write. File-size limits are not stated in the API docs (they defer to Canva Help upload requirements).

Canva Help upload limits for PDF import: up to 300 MB and 500 pages (~1,400 elements); unsupported fonts are replaced with the closest Canva font; scanned PDFs import as flattened images; text and images become separate editable elements. Whether PDF link annotations survive import is not stated. Help Center pages returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher; these figures come from search-result snippets of canva.com/help pages and third-party write-ups.
claims.source: https://www.canva.com/help/upload-formats-requirements/ and https://www.canva.com/help/import-and-edit-pdfs-canva/ (403 on fetch; figures via search snippets)

claims.claim: Folders: POST /v1/folders creates a folder under 'root', 'uploads' or a parent folder id (20 req/min/user, scope folder:write); also Get/Update/Delete folder, List folder items, Move folder item. No plan gate stated.

Autofill API: 'To use the Autofill APIs, your integration must act on behalf of a user who is a member of a Canva Enterprise organization. Users on Canva paid plans have access to a limited trial while your integration is under development.' Fields: text, image (video as image), chart (≤100 rows x 20 cols), sheet; strings ≤ 10,000 chars; ≤ 20 media items per cell; unknown field names silently skipped; 60 req/min/user; scope design:content:write. Job types create_from_brand_template, create_from_design, update_design (GA 2026-08-25).
claims.gate: Enterprise for production; 'limited trial' for paid plans during development (extent of trial not quantified)

claims.claim: Brand Templates API (list/get/dataset/publish): 'your integration must act on behalf of a user that's on a Canva plan with access to brand templates (such as Canva Pro, Canva Teams, or Canva Enterprise)'; 100 req/min/user; scope brandtemplate:meta:read.
Get design pages (GET /v1/designs/{id}/pages) is 'currently provided as a preview'; returns page thumbnails/dimensions/ids only, not elements; 100 req/min/user.

Rate limits are documented per endpoint (no global page exists): create design 20/min, asset upload 30/min, export 20/min (+ the quotas above), import 20/min, folders 20/min, autofill 60/min, brand templates 100/min, users/me 10/min, comments list 100/min — all 'for each user of your integration'. Poll async jobs with exponential backoff.
claims.source: https://www.canva.dev/docs/connect/api-requests-responses/ plus the per-endpoint pages cited above

claims.claim: Canva remote MCP server (https://mcp.canva.com/mcp) plan availability: 'All plans: Design generation, editing, search, exports, comments, asset uploads, and most core features'; 'Canva Pro and above: Design resizing'; 'Enterprise: Autofill templates, brand kits, brand templates'. Editing tools: start-editing-transaction (returns element ids for 'richtexts and fills'), perform-editing-operations, commit-editing-transaction; documented operations are replace_text and find_and_replace_text; images must be uploaded first with upload-asset-from-url (public HTTPS URL, 30 req/min) to get an asset_id. Editing transactions 20–100 req/min; export-design 20/min; import-design-from-url 20/min.

Third-party pages claim the MCP edit tool 'now supports text insertion and page insertion' and reads geometry — this was NOT found on canva.dev; the canva.dev operation docs show only text replacement on existing elements. Treat coordinate-level placement of new text/images via MCP as unverified.
claims.source: canva.dev MCP tool pages (above) vs search snippets citing docs.dust.tt / canva.com/help/mcp-canva-usage (403 on fetch)

claims.claim: Connecting one's OWN MCP client (e.g. a Python agent) to mcp.canva.com requires the redirect URI to be allowlisted via a Waitlist form reviewed for 'brand alignment, trust and safety considerations, compliance readiness, technical fit, and strategic alignment'; 'Private access is currently limited as we have a full waitlist of clients.' Pre-configured access exists for 'ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Grok, Perplexity, Superhuman, and more' (canva.dev also names Gemini, Cursor, VS Code). Claude Code specifically: not named on canva.dev pages read.
claims.gate: waitlist for custom clients; self-serve only through pre-approved assistants

claims.claim: Newsroom pages (canva.com/newsroom/...) and Help Center pages (canva.com/help/...) returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher; claims sourced from them are marked could-not-verify or rely on canva.dev equivalents.

Summary of what an individual Canva Pro user can use TODAY via Connect without Enterprise: OAuth into a public-in-draft integration (no review), Asset Upload, Create Design (blank, or blank + one image), Design Import (PDF / .ai / PPTX), Export (PDF regular or pro), Folders, Brand Templates (read/list), Get design/list designs, Comments, Webhooks. NOT usable: Private integrations (Enterprise), Autofill in production (Enterprise; dev-time 'limited trial' only), any element-level editing (does not exist in Connect).
claims.source: Aggregate of the canva.dev pages cited above

steps_for_this_kit: 1. In Luke's Chrome, open canva.dev Developer Portal > Your integrations > Create an integration > PUBLIC (leave in draft; never submit). Name it, add redirect URL http://127.0.0.1:3001/oauth/redirect, tick scopes asset (R/W), design:content (R/W), design:meta (R), folder (R/W), brandtemplate:meta (R). Generate client secret once and store it locally (never in the repo).

2. Run a tiny local OAuth PKCE receiver (Python, port 3001). Agent opens the authorize URL in Luke's logged-in Chrome; Luke clicks Allow; receiver exchanges the code for an access token (4 h) + single-use refresh token. Persist tokens locally; refresh on 401.

3. Connect: POST /v1/folders to create 'KILLER OF MEN — EPK' under root and a 'Press assets' subfolder. Then POST /v1/asset-uploads for the poster JPG, 41 stills (1920x1080 PNG), 10 BTS JPGs and 4 headshots — all under 50 MB each; throttle to <30/min (56 files ≈ 2–3 min). Optionally move uploaded assets into the subfolder with Move folder item. Record every asset_id → filename in a JSON manifest.

4. Baseline design — two documented options, run both and compare: (a) Design Import: POST /v1/imports with the 9.8 MB compressed EPK PDF (or the .ai) → editable design(s); check page count (11), whether text landed as editable text, fonts substituted, and whether the 19 links survived (unverified). (b) Create Design: POST /v1/designs with custom 1296x1728 px (fits the 25 M px² cap) — this yields ONE blank page only; Connect cannot add pages or content.

5. Content placement is NOT possible through Connect. Choose the placement surface and flag it plainly to Luke: (i) Apps SDK app run via Developer Portal 'Preview' (no review, no stated plan gate) from the agent's local dev server — port build-epk-kit.py's operations list to addPage() calls (custom 1296x1728 page; text with fontRef + link; images by asset ref) for pages 2–11 and openDesign for page 1; fonts: resolve Baskerville via findFonts/requestFontSelection first and fall back if absent; or (ii) drive the Canva editor UI directly with Claude-in-Chrome (the browser lane); or (iii) Canva AI Connector from a pre-approved assistant (text replacement documented; insertion unverified). Recommendation: (i) for fidelity, (ii) as fallback.

6. Verification: GET /v1/designs/{id}/pages (preview API, thumbnails) to eyeball each page; POST /v1/exports {format:'pdf', export_quality:'pro'} and diff the exported PDF against the Illustrator master (page size, text positions, link annotations) with the Python toolchain. Stay under 20 exports/min and 75 per 5 min per document.

7. Hand-off: share the Canva design/folder with the director and producer from Luke's account (sharing is not exposed in the Connect scopes list read; do it in the UI). Revoke the integration token (POST /v1/oauth/revoke) when finished.
limits: Connect cannot place text, images, rules or hyperlinks on a page, cannot add pages, and cannot set fonts — the only content it can inject is one image asset at design creation and whatever Design Import extracts from a PDF/.ai.
Private integrations are Enterprise-only; the workable route for a Pro user is a public integration left in draft (documented as allowed for 'individual usage and testing').
Autofill (Brand Templates → designs) requires Enterprise in production; Pro gets only an unquantified 'limited trial while your integration is under development'.
Create-design custom size is in pixels (max 8000 per side, 25,000,000 px² area) — 18x24 in must be expressed as 1296x1728 px (72 px/in); Canva has no inch/pt unit in this endpoint.

Export PDF has no CMYK, bleed, crop-mark or flatten options; PDF 'size' paper presets apply only to Canva Docs; 'pro' quality may fail if premium elements are present on a plan without premium features.
Asset uploads capped at 50 MB per image, 30 req/min; asset names ≤ 50 characters (unencoded).

Design Import: imports 'with a large number of pages or assets are split into multiple designs'; font substitution and link-annotation survival are not documented on canva.dev (Help Center pages returned 403).
Blank designs created via the API are auto-deleted if not edited within 7 days.
Access tokens last 4 h; refresh tokens are single-use — a lost refresh response forces re-authorization by Luke in the browser.
Get design pages (thumbnail verification) is a preview API.

Apps SDK Design Editing (the only programmatic element-level surface): all_pages is preview; sessions expire after 1 minute; image URLs passed to upload() must be public HTTPS (the agent needs a public URL, e.g. the Drive mirror or a tunnel, not localhost); findFonts returns only a subset of fonts, and Baskerville availability is unverified.
Custom MCP clients need waitlist approval; documented MCP edit operations are text replacement only.
effort_estimate: Connect-only work (integration setup, OAuth receiver, 56 asset uploads, folder, PDF/.ai import, PDF export + diff): about half a day of agent time plus two Luke clicks (Allow in OAuth; confirm import result). Rebuilding the eleven pages with true text, fonts and 19 links requires the Apps SDK placement step: roughly 1–2 days to port build-epk-kit.py's operation list to addPage()/openDesign calls, run the app via Developer Portal Preview from a local dev server, resolve fonts, and iterate on pixel positions; add a day if Baskerville must be substituted and re-kerned. Browser-driven placement as fallback is slower (hours per page) and less exact.
fidelity_to_the_pdf: Via Connect alone: low-to-medium. Design Import is the only path that yields text and images on 11 pages, and Canva rebuilds the layout with its own type engine, substitutes non-library fonts, and (undocumented) may drop PDF link annotations; splitting into multiple designs is possible. Via Apps SDK addPage driven from the existing operations list: medium-to-high — text runs with fontRef, size, colour (#efe6d6 on #0b0806 backgrounds), alignment and per-range hyperlinks are all documented, images place by asset ref at pixel coordinates, page size 1296x1728 px matches 18x24 in at 72 px/in; residual gaps are Baskerville availability/metrics, rules drawn as thin rects or shapes, and Canva's own text-box wrapping versus Illustrator's. Exported PDF quality: 'pro' export, no print-production controls.

lane: Canva Apps SDK (an app running inside the Canva editor, canva.dev/docs/apps) — feasibility of replaying the build-epk-kit.py operation list into an 18 x 24 in Canva design

claims.claim: Anyone with a standard (free) Canva account has full access to the Developer Portal; no separate developer account or paid plan is required. Creating an app requires agreeing to the Canva Developer Terms.

Toolchain: the starter kit / `canva apps create` requires Node.js v24 and npm v11; `canva apps start` serves the bundle at http://localhost:8080. The app is previewed by setting App source > Development URL in the Developer Portal to that localhost URL and clicking Preview; Chrome works over plain HTTP, Safari needs `--use-https`. You cannot open localhost:8080 directly; the app only renders inside the Canva editor.

No review is needed for the owner to run the app in preview/development mode. Review is only required to release: public release goes through Canva's app review; 'team apps' (private distribution to a team) are only available to teams on an Enterprise plan and are approved by a team owner/admin instead of Canva. Consequence: Luke can run the app himself in preview; the director/producer cannot run the app (not Enterprise) but they do not need to — they edit the resulting design.
claims.gate: Team-app distribution = Canva Enterprise only; public distribution = Canva review. Owner-only preview use = no gate.
claims.source: https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/managing-team-apps.md ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/releasing-apps.md ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/previewing-apps.md ('You can't submit an app for review while the [Development URL] field contains a value')

claims.claim: Whether the Preview button can open the app inside an EXISTING design (vs. a new preview design) and whether the design type/size can be chosen at preview time is not stated in the docs; the docs only say Preview 'opens the app in a preview Canva editor' in a new tab and lets you pick the intent to preview.

`addElementAtPoint` (from @canva/design) places elements at absolute top/left (and width/height for images) in fixed-dimension designs (posters, presentations); it does NOT work in Docs/Whiteboards. Supported positioned element types: image, video, embed, text, richtext, shape, group, table. Coordinate ranges: top/left -32768..32767, width/height 0..32767, rotation -180..180. Units are pixels of the design; origin is the page's top-left.
claims.source: https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/api/latest/design-add-element-at-point/ ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/elements/ (support table lists Richtext under addElementAtPoint) ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/positioning-elements.md

claims.claim: Plain `text` elements accept: children (one string), fontSize 1..1000 (px in API, shown as pt in UI), color (#rrggbb), textAlign start|center|end|justify, fontWeight normal|thin|extralight|light|medium|semibold|bold|ultrabold|heavy, fontStyle normal|italic, decoration none|underline, fontRef, width, rotation. They have NO letter-spacing, NO line-height, NO link property, and 'Text elements can't have a predefined height' / 'Apps can't set the line-height of text'.

`richtext` elements (createRichtextRange + type:'richtext' with range, top, left, optional width) DO support tracking and leading and links: formatParagraph accepts fontRef, fontSize, textAlign, letterSpacingEm (range -0.2..0.8 em, default 0), lineHeightEm (0.5..2.5, default 1.4), list props; formatText (inline) accepts color, fontWeight, fontStyle, decoration, strikethrough, and `link` ('An external URL that the text links to'). letterSpacingEm/lineHeightEm went GA in @canva/design 2.11.0 on 2026-08-10. Font can only be set per paragraph, not inline.
claims.source: https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/api/latest/design-create-richtext-range/ ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/examples/richtext-elements/ (shows RichtextElementAtPoint with top/left/width and formatParagraph letterSpacingEm) ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/api/latest/design-changelog.md (2.11.0, 2026-08-10) ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/fonts.md ('Apps can only set the font of paragraphs, not of inline text')

claims.claim: Fonts are referenced by an opaque FontRef obtained either from `requestFontSelection()` (opens Canva's own font picker; returns ref, name, available weights/styles) or `findFonts()` (returns 'a subset of Canva's fonts'; also resolves specific refs via {fontRefs:[...]}). A ref can be hard-coded once discovered. Hard limits: 'Apps can't access Canva Pro fonts', 'Apps can't upload or otherwise define custom fonts', 'Apps can't download the underlying font files'.

Whether a Brand Kit UPLOADED font (e.g. Luke's Baskerville) appears in the app's requestFontSelection picker or in findFonts, and whether such a ref can be applied to elements, is not documented anywhere in the Apps SDK docs (brand kit / uploaded fonts are never mentioned). Uploading fonts to a Brand Kit is itself gated to Pro/Teams/Business/Education/Nonprofits (OTF/TTF/WOFF, 500 fonts per kit, must be licensed for embedding). Must be tested at runtime on Luke's account.
claims.gate: Brand Kit font upload = Canva Pro or higher (help center); app access to those fonts = undocumented
claims.source: https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/fonts.md (silent) ; https://www.canva.com/help/upload-fonts/ (plan list, via search snippet — page itself returned 403 to fetch)

claims.claim: Canva's library does not carry Monotype Baskerville; the free look-alike is Libre Baskerville (Regular/Italic/Bold only, no SemiBold weight in the family). Both statements come from secondary sources; Canva's own 'best free business fonts' page (canva.com/learn) was returned in search as listing Libre Baskerville as free but returned 403 to fetch.

Images: `upload()` from @canva/asset takes type:'image', mimeType (jpeg/png/webp/svg/heic/tiff), aiDisclosure, and a `url` that is either an HTTPS URL that 'Must be publicly accessible (i.e. not a localhost URL)', 'Must not redirect', 'Must not contain an IP address', max 50MB — or a base64 data URL, 'Maximum size: 10MB (10 × 1024 × 1024 characters)'. Returns {ref, whenUploaded()}. Image elements can also be placed directly with a `dataUrl` instead of a ref. Consequence: a localhost dev server cannot be an image source; Google Drive share links redirect and so fail; the practical path is data URLs generated from Python (pre-cropped, re-encoded under 10MB).

No crop box or opacity can be set when ADDING an image via addElementAtPoint/addPage (ImageElementAtPoint has only ref/dataUrl, altText, top, left, width, height, rotation). In the Design Editing API, images are 'rects with fills'; ImageFill exposes flipX/flipY only, no crop. Element-level `transparency` is a common editable property in the Design Editing API (per the design-editing page text surfaced in search; not re-confirmed on a direct fetch). Consequence: the kit's cover-crops must be baked into the uploaded pixels, and the 16%-opacity ghost stills either baked in or set post-hoc via openDesign().transparency.

`addPage(opts)` adds a page with optional title (≤255 chars), background (solid hex / image / video), `elements` (ElementAtPoint[] incl. richtext) and `dimensions` {width,height} in px: each side 40..8000, total area ≤ 25,000,000 px². Returns {id, title, dimensions, type}. Custom dimensions added in 2.7.5 (2025-12-09); page IDs in 2.12.0 (2026-08-12). Canva's editor imposes the same envelope: designs min 40 x 40 px, max 8000 x 3125 px (help center).
claims.source: https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/api/latest/design-add-page.md ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/api/latest/design-changelog.md ; https://www.canva.com/help/resize/ (via search snippet; page 403 on fetch)

claims.claim: Page size in Canva px for an 18 x 24 in poster: Canva help/docs do not publish the in→px factor. Secondary sources say Canva converts at 96 px/in, which gives 1728 x 2304 px (area 3.98M, inside the 25M addPage cap). A 300-dpi interpretation (5400 x 7200, area 38.9M) would exceed both the addPage area cap and the editor's 8000 x 3125 max, so it cannot be what Canva stores. The agent must read the real value at runtime with getDesignMetadata().defaultPageDimensions / getCurrentPageContext().dimensions (both documented as pixels) and scale the kit's 1296 x 1728 pt layout by pagePx/1296, flipping y (PDF origin bottom-left → Canva top-left).
claims.source: https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/api/latest/design-get-design-metadata/ ; https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/api/latest/design-get-current-page-context/ ; https://www.canva.com/help/resize/ (8000x3125 max, via search snippet) ; 96 px/in from secondary sites only

claims.claim: Reading the current design: `openDesign({type:'current_page'|'all_pages'}, cb)` from @canva/design reads and edits pages (dimensions, elements, text as richtext, rect fills, transparency); GA since 2.6.1 (2025-06-24), multi-page GA since 2.10.0 (2026-06-12) — although the narrative design-editing page still says all_pages is 'in preview', so the docs are internally inconsistent. Sessions expire after 1 minute; edits apply only on sync(). The Design Editing API 'cannot add pages'.

Hyperlinks: via the API only on TEXT, through richtext inline `link`. There is no link property on image, shape or group elements in addElementAtPoint/addPage, and the @canva/design changelog has no entry adding one. In the editor UI, Canva lets users add links to text, elements, images and videos, and they survive PDF download (non-flattened). So any of the 19 links that sit on an image rather than on words must be added by hand (or by the browser agent) after the build.
Rules/lines: no line element; use a `shape` element (viewBox + SVG paths, 1–30 paths, ≤2 KB combined, ≤6 fill colours) drawn as a thin filled rectangle at exact top/left/width/height.

Rate limits: none are published for addElementAtPoint, addPage, upload, findFonts or openDesign (each reference page was checked; only requestExport has a documented limit). A `rate_limited` CanvaError code exists ('too many requests within a certain time period'), so the replayer must await each call and back off on that code.

Element-count ceiling: a '1,000 unique elements per design' warning is reported by secondary sites; the Canva help center documents an element limit only for Whiteboards ('Too many elements'). The kit (~11 pages, several hundred text runs + ~60 images) is likely under it, but per-line text emission could approach it.

steps_for_this_kit: 0. Luke, in Chrome: log into canva.com; open https://www.canva.dev (Developer Portal), accept the Developer Terms once; if he is on Pro, upload Baskerville Regular/SemiBold/Bold (OTF/TTF) to his Brand Kit so the font-availability test in step 4 can be run.

1. Agent, Python: add a `--canva-json` mode to tools/build-epk-ai.py's recording canvas that dumps the op list as JSON in Canva terms: page index; text runs (string, font key, size pt, tracking pt, colour, x, y baseline, align, width for paragraphs); rules (x,y,w,h); images (path + crop box + alpha + target box); links (url + rect). Convert on emit: scale = pagePx/1296 (read pagePx at runtime, do not hardcode 1728x2304), y_canva = (1728 - y_pt - ascent)*scale, tracking_em = track_pt/size_pt, lead_em = lead/size. Group each paragraph into one richtext op (not one op per line) so the director/producer get editable paragraphs; keep one-line ops for titles/labels.

2. Agent, Python/PIL: render every image op to a derived JPEG/PNG: cover-crop to the box, downsample to ≤ 2x target px, bake the 0.16-alpha ghost + 0.55 scrim into the pixels for page 4 grounds, re-encode until the base64 data URL is < 10 MB. Never touch the masters. Write them next to the JSON.

3. Agent, Node 24: `npm i -g @canva/cli`, `canva apps create kom-epk-builder` (React starter), `canva apps start` on :8080. In the Developer Portal set App source > Development URL = http://localhost:8080 (Chrome, no HTTPS needed). The app UI: a file input to load the JSON (the browser reads it, so no public URL is required), a 'Pick font' button, and 'Build' / 'Build page N' buttons plus a log pane.

4. Font test (decides fidelity): in the preview editor, click 'Pick font' → requestFontSelection(). Check whether the Brand Kit Baskerville appears; if it does, record its ref, weights and styles; if not, search 'Libre Baskerville' and record that ref (expect normal + bold only; map SemiBold → bold and note it). Persist the ref in the app config. Also log getDesignMetadata().defaultPageDimensions to confirm the px size of the 18 x 24 in poster preset.

5. Create the target design: because it is unverified that Preview can attach to an existing design, first test it: Portal → Preview; if the editor opens a fresh design, use the editor's Resize / File > Custom size to 18 x 24 in (or let the app addPage with dimensions {width:1728,height:2304} px if the runtime confirms 96 px/in and delete the default page by hand). Fall back to opening the app from the editor's Apps panel in a design Luke created at 18 x 24 in, if it appears there.

6. Build loop, per page: (a) addPage({title, dimensions, background:{color:'#0b0806'}}); (b) for each image op: upload({type:'image', url: dataURL, mimeType, aiDisclosure:'none', width, height}) → await whenUploaded → addElementAtPoint({type:'image', ref, altText, top, left, width, height}); (c) each rule → shape element (rect path, fill #rule-colour); (d) each text op → createRichtextRange(); appendText; formatParagraph({fontRef, fontSize, textAlign, letterSpacingEm, lineHeightEm}); formatText for colour/weight and for any `link` span → addElementAtPoint({type:'richtext', range, top, left, width}); (e) await every call sequentially, catch CanvaError 'rate_limited' and retry with backoff. Log element counts per page.

7. Post-pass with openDesign({type:'all_pages'}) to (a) read back element positions and dump them for a diff against the JSON, (b) set transparency on any element that needs it instead of baked alpha, (c) confirm the page order (order not guaranteed by getDesignMetadata; use the page ids returned by addPage).

8. Links that sit on images (not on words): have the Claude-in-Chrome agent select each image and add the URL via the editor's link control, from the recorded link list; then Share > Download > PDF Standard (not flattened) and verify link annotations with pypdf against the 19 expected URLs.

9. QA: export PDF, rasterise side-by-side with press/KillerOfMen_EPK_1234_10092026_compressed.pdf page by page, diff text positions and line breaks; fix by tightening width or font size in the JSON, rebuild the affected page only. Then share the design with the director and producer as editors (their plan tier is irrelevant for editing).
limits: Fonts: the app cannot upload or define fonts and cannot use Canva Pro fonts; Brand Kit uploaded fonts appearing in the app's picker is undocumented and must be tested. Likely fallback is Libre Baskerville (no SemiBold weight).

Plain text elements have no tracking/leading/link; everything with tracking, leading or a link must be a richtext element (letterSpacingEm -0.2..0.8, lineHeightEm 0.5..2.5); font is per paragraph only.

Text elements cannot be given a height and Canva reflows lines with its own engine, so line breaks will not match reportlab's exactly unless each line is emitted as its own element (which hurts editability and inflates element count).

Images: no crop box and no opacity at creation; crops/ghosting must be baked into the uploaded pixels (opacity can be set afterwards via openDesign transparency). Upload source must be a public HTTPS non-redirecting URL (<50 MB) or a data URL (<10 MB); localhost and Google Drive share links do not qualify.
Hyperlinks on images/shapes cannot be set via the Apps SDK (text-only via richtext link); they must be added in the editor UI.

Page geometry: addPage sides 40..8000 px and area ≤ 25,000,000 px²; editor max 8000 x 3125 px. The exact px size Canva assigns to 18 x 24 in is unpublished (probably 1728 x 2304 at 96 px/in) — read it at runtime.
addElementAtPoint/addPage only work in fixed-dimension designs (fine for a poster); Design Editing API cannot add pages.

Distribution: the app can only be run by Luke in development/preview mode; sharing the app itself with teammates requires Canva Enterprise; public release requires Canva review. Collaborators edit the resulting design, not the app.
Whether Preview can open the app inside an existing design is undocumented; step 5 tests it.

No published rate limits for the calls used; a `rate_limited` error code exists, so the replayer must be sequential with backoff. A ~1,000-elements-per-design ceiling is reported by secondary sources only.

Toolchain: Node 24 / npm 11 required; Chrome recommended (Safari needs HTTPS dev server). Both canva.com/help pages and canva.com/sizes returned 403 to automated fetch, so help-center facts above were taken from search snippets of those pages.
effort_estimate: Roughly 2–3 agent working days: 0.5 day for the JSON emitter and image derivation in Python (reusing build-epk-ai.py's recording canvas), 1 day for the React app (upload → addPage → richtext/shape/image placement, font picker, backoff, read-back), 0.5 day for the font/preview/page-size runtime tests that decide fidelity, 0.5–1 day for QA diffs against the PDF, manual image links, and Luke's review passes. Risk-weighted: if Brand Kit Baskerville is not exposed to apps, add a half day for a Libre Baskerville re-fit of the type (widths change).
fidelity_to_the_pdf: Good but not pixel-identical. Positions, sizes, colours, rules, image crops and text links can all be reproduced from the same coordinates the PDF and .ai use (scaled to Canva px, y flipped). Expected deviations: (1) typeface — Baskerville only if Luke's Brand Kit upload is reachable by the app (unverified); otherwise Libre Baskerville, which is visibly different and lacks SemiBold; (2) line breaks in running text will drift because Canva reflows richtext with its own metrics, unless lines are emitted one per element; (3) tracking/leading are clamped to -0.2..0.8 em and 0.5..2.5 em (the kit's values fit); (4) the 16 % ghost stills are baked pixels rather than live opacity unless set in a second openDesign pass; (5) image-borne links are added by hand; (6) the page is stored at Canva's screen-px size for 18 x 24 in, so Canva's own 'Print PDF' export governs output resolution rather than the 300-dpi masters. Everything the collaborators would want to edit (paragraph copy, bios, credits, links on text) remains live text in Canva.

Charts, SmartArt, 3D objects, WordArt ignored. Fonts: 'We'll try to identify and match the text font... it's not always possible to find an exact match.' Scans import flat. Hyperlink handling and slide-size preservation are not documented.

Illustrator (.ai) route, relevant because the kit exists as .ai: beta, desktop only; 'You can only import Illustrator designs saved as PDF compatible format'; size limit stated as 100 MB on the ai-import page but 300 MB on the formats page (conflict); up to 300 artboards per design, up to 100 fonts, 1,200 images per page; 'layers, gradients, and masks are supported, but some elements might be rasterized'; fonts matched approximately. Handling of linked (not embedded) images is not documented; PDF-compatible saving embeds a rendition, but verify visually.

Connect API design import exists: POST design import job (octet-stream body + Import-Metadata header with base64 title <=50 chars, optional mime_type), URL import job (public URL), and GET job status. Supported types include application/pdf, PPTX/PPT, .ai, .psd, Affinity, Keynote/Pages, Word, ODF. Scope design:content:write; 20 create requests/min/user; 'Imports with a large number of pages or assets are split into multiple designs.' No fidelity, font, link or size behaviour documented — it is the same converter behind the UI, as far as the docs say.

Connect API access: creating an integration requires a Canva account with MFA enabled. 'Public integrations are available to all Canva users, but the integration must first be reviewed by Canva'; 'Private integrations can only be used by your team on a Canva Enterprise plan.' Whether a developer can authorize an unreviewed public integration against their own account (quickstart uses http://127.0.0.1:3001/oauth/redirect, implying local testing) is not explicitly stated. For an 11-page kit the UI upload is sufficient; the API adds nothing to fidelity.

Alt text embedded in imported PDFs and PPTXs is preserved and included in exports (only import-preservation statement Canva makes about PDF metadata). Export for links: Share > Download > PDF, preset Digital, Flatten PDF unchecked.
Storage: Free 5 GB, Pro 100 GB per the formats page (another help article says Pro/Teams 1 TB — conflicting). Irrelevant at this kit's size but noted as a doc inconsistency.

Route verdict: PDF import is the most editable path for this kit. SVG gives no text. PPTX would require first generating a PPTX from the Python layout and is documented as beta with approximate font matching and no link documentation — no advantage over PDF. .ai import is a fallback if PDF text fragments badly (it carries the same text runs but also the same font-matching caveat and no hyperlinks).

steps_for_this_kit: 0. Decide the font question with Luke before touching Canva: (a) split Apple Baskerville.ttc into Regular/SemiBold/Bold .ttf and upload to Brand Kit (needs Pro; licensing of Apple's bundled font for upload is unverified and is Luke's call), or (b) accept Libre Baskerville from Canva's library (verify it exists in the font picker), or (c) buy/obtain a licensed Baskerville in TTF/OTF. Do not upload the .ttc as-is; Canva accepts only OTF/TTF/WOFF under 15 MB.

1. Generate an import-optimized PDF from build-epk-kit.py rather than importing the compressed one: images at full resolution (the compressed PDF already holds 1663 px BTS and 1920 px stills), keep total under 300 MB, and, if feasible, emit tracked caps as single text runs with character spacing instead of per-glyph draws so Canva has a chance to keep one text box per line. Keep 1296 x 1728 pt page size and embedded TrueType text (confirm with pdffonts).
2. In Luke's logged-in Chrome (agent-driven): Canva Home > Upload > Upload files > pick the PDF; wait for 'imported' state; open the design. Menu path per Canva help, read 2026-09-10.

3. Audit immediately, page by page, before any edits: (a) Resize > Custom size shows 18 x 24 in (if not, Resize this design to 18 x 24 in — Pro, uses an AI-usage credit); (b) count text boxes vs the 11-page text-run list from build-epk-kit.py, note fragmentation; (c) note which font Canva substituted; (d) check whether any of the 19 links survived (expect none); (e) check images were separated, not flattened with the dark ground.

4. Fonts: set every text box to the chosen Baskerville (uploaded family appears under 'Uploaded fonts'; SemiBold/Bold are separate uploaded styles). No documented font-wide replace tool; drive it per text box or per-page select-all where styles match. Re-check tracking (Advanced settings > Spacing) on the caps labels.

5. Images: upload the originals from FESTIVAL CAMPAIGN/site/press/assets (each under 50 MB / 250 MP) to Uploads and drag each onto its imported placeholder so it replaces in place; keep crops identical to the PDF.
6. Links: re-add all 19 (select text/element > More > Link > paste URL) from the link list emitted by build-epk-kit.py; mailto and https both supported as URLs.

7. Verify by export: Share > Download > PDF (Digital), Flatten PDF off, all pages; open the exported PDF and run pdffonts / link count (expect 19 /Link annots) / pdfimages against the source PDF; visually diff page renders (pdftoppm both, side by side) before handing to collaborators.

8. Share the design with the director and producer as editors (collaborator editing does not require them to be on Pro for the fonts to render in the shared design, but that is not verified here — check after sharing).
limits: PDF import: 300 MB, 500 pages, 1,400 elements+images per file; scanned/outlined text imports flat.
PPTX import: 300 MB (.pptx), 300 slides, 1,400 elements; beta; charts/SmartArt/3D/WordArt dropped.
SVG upload: under 3 MB, 150-200 px wide, SVG 1.1, text must be expanded — no editable text, no design import.
.ai import: PDF-compatible saves only; 100 MB (ai-import page) vs 300 MB (formats page) conflict; 300 artboards; 100 fonts; 1,200 images/page; some elements rasterized.
Fonts: upload is Pro-and-above; OTF/TTF/WOFF only, under 15 MB, no variable fonts, no TTC; must be licensed for embedding; 500 per Brand Kit; 18 styles per family.
Design size: each side 40-8000 px (help pages also print '8000 x 3125 px'); 18 x 24 in is a listed poster preset; Resize is Pro-and-above and counts against monthly AI usage.
Images: under 50 MB and under 250 million pixels each.
Hyperlinks: work only in non-flattened PDF downloads; preservation through import is undocumented (expect to re-add 19).
Canva help pages return 403 to non-browser fetchers (WebFetch, curl); all help-center reads here were via a real browser tab on 2026-09-10.
Not tested live: no import was performed against Luke's account; everything about fragmentation, substituted font, and page-size survival is documented-or-inferred, not observed.
effort_estimate: Import itself: minutes. Cleanup is the cost: font reassignment across 11 pages (tens to low hundreds of text boxes depending on fragmentation), 19 links re-added, ~56 image replacements if originals are swapped in, plus a verification export. Agent-driven in Chrome with Luke checking pages: roughly 2-4 hours; longer if tracked caps import as per-glyph boxes and pages need partial rebuild. Add 30-60 minutes up front for the font-licence decision and building an import-optimized PDF.
fidelity_to_the_pdf: Expect layout positions and the dark ground to survive, real text to import as editable boxes (possibly fragmented where letters are tracked), fonts to be substituted until manually reassigned (exact Baskerville only if a licensed TTF/OTF can be uploaded on Pro; otherwise Libre Baskerville, a visibly different cut), images to arrive at the PDF's embedded pixel size (so replace from originals), and all 19 hyperlinks to need re-adding. Page size survival at 18 x 24 in is unverified; correctable with Resize on Pro. Net: a faithful-looking but not pixel-identical kit, editable by collaborators, after a manual pass.
